items.stem: Under IFRS 15, when should revenue from a contract with a customer be recognised?

options.text: When (or as) each performance obligation is satisfied by transferring control of a good or service
options.rationale: Correct: IFRS 15 recognises revenue as performance obligations are satisfied through the transfer of control.

options.text: When the customer's cash is received
options.rationale: Cash receipt is not the recognition trigger; revenue follows transfer of control.
Signing a contract alone does not transfer control of any good or service.

options.text: Evenly over the entity's financial year
options.rationale: Straight-line over the year is not a basis in IFRS 15 unless it reflects satisfaction of an obligation.

items.explanation: Correct: IFRS 15 recognises revenue as performance obligations are satisfied through the transfer of control.

items.stem: Under IFRS 16, how does a lessee generally account for a lease (other than short-term or low-value leases) at commencement?

options.text: Recognise a right-of-use asset and a corresponding lease liability
options.rationale: Correct: IFRS 16 requires lessees to recognise a right-of-use asset and a lease liability for most leases.

options.text: Charge all payments to profit or loss as an operating expense with no asset or liability
options.rationale: That is the superseded operating-lease treatment; IFRS 16 removed it for lessees except for exemptions.

options.text: Recognise the leased asset at its full market value and no liability
options.rationale: The asset is measured at the lease liability plus certain costs, and a liability is recognised.

options.text: Recognise only a liability and no asset
options.rationale: A right-of-use asset is recognised alongside the liability.

items.explanation: Correct: IFRS 16 requires lessees to recognise a right-of-use asset and a lease liability for most leases.

items.stem: Select TWO conditions that must both be met for an investor to consolidate an investee as a subsidiary under IFRS 10.

options.text: The investor has power over the investee
options.rationale: Correct: power over the relevant activities of the investee is a control criterion.

options.text: The investor is exposed to variable returns from its involvement
options.rationale: Correct: exposure or rights to variable returns is a control criterion.

options.text: The investor holds exactly 50% of the voting shares
options.rationale: Control is about power and returns, not a fixed 50% shareholding.

options.text: The investee operates in the same country as the investor
options.rationale: Geography is irrelevant to the control assessment.

options.text: The investor accounts for the investee using the equity method
options.rationale: The equity method applies to associates, not consolidated subsidiaries.

items.explanation: Correct: power over the relevant activities of the investee is a control criterion.
